source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.3.5, first sentence and displayed inequality
source_evidence.observation: The exercise invokes the setting of Theorem 2.3.1 and asks to show, for delta in (0,1], the two-sided estimate P{|S_N - mu| >= delta mu} <= 2 exp(-c mu delta^2), where c > 0 is an absolute constant.
The inherited setting consists of independent Bernoulli random variables X_i with parameters p_i, their sum S_N = sum_{i=1}^N X_i, and its mean mu = E[S_N].

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 2.3.1, paragraph beginning 'Since X_i takes value 1'
source_evidence.observation: The source's Bernoulli convention is explicit in the proof: X_i equals 1 with probability p_i and 0 with probability 1-p_i.

source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.3.1 displayed bound and Exercise 2.3.2 displayed bound
source_evidence.observation: The referenced one-sided estimates are P{S_N >= t} <= exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t for t > mu and P{S_N <= t} <= exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t for t < mu.
The suggested derivation applies Theorem 2.3.1 and Exercise 2.3.2 at t = (1 plus or minus delta)mu and analyzes the resulting bounds for small delta.

binders: A finite family X_1, ..., X_N of random variables and Bernoulli parameters p_1, ..., p_N, inherited from Theorem 2.3.1 (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 opening sentence).
A real deviation parameter delta, universally quantified subject to delta in (0,1] (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5 first sentence).

A positive absolute real constant c, existentially asserted uniformly over the problem data by the phrase 'where c > 0 is an absolute constant' (PDF page 9, printed page 20, after the displayed inequality).
hypotheses: The X_i are mutually independent Bernoulli random variables with respective parameters p_i (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 opening sentence).
S_N is the sum of the X_i and mu is its expectation (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 opening sentence).
The deviation parameter satisfies 0 < delta <= 1 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5 first sentence).
conclusions: The probability of the inclusive two-sided event |S_N - mu| >= delta mu is at most 2 exp(-c mu delta^2) (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5 displayed inequality).
definitions_and_conventions: S_N := sum_{i=1}^N X_i and mu := E[S_N] (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 opening sentence).
Under the source's Bernoulli convention, X_i takes value 1 with probability p_i and value 0 with probability 1-p_i (PDF page 8, printed page 19, proof of Theorem 2.3.1).

The adjective 'absolute' makes c independent of N, the Bernoulli parameters, the chosen variables, and delta; the source does not specify a numerical value (PDF page 9, printed page 20, phrase 'c > 0 is an absolute constant').
implicit_context: All probabilities and expectations are taken in the ambient probability space carrying the independent variables (PDF page 8, printed pages 18-19, Theorem 2.3.1 and its probability/MGF proof).
The family need not be identically distributed: the source assigns a possibly different parameter p_i to each X_i (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 opening sentence).
The conclusion inherits the entire setting of Theorem 2.3.1 rather than restating it locally (PDF page 9, printed page 20, phrase 'in the setting of Theorem 2.3.1').

details: One numerical c > 0 must work uniformly for every admissible finite independent Bernoulli family and every delta in (0,1] (PDF page 9, printed page 20, phrase 'absolute constant').
The event is two-sided and uses an inclusive threshold: |S_N - mu| >= delta mu (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
The scale delta mu is relative to the mean, not an arbitrary additive threshold (same displayed inequality).
The exponent has quadratic dependence on delta and linear dependence on mu: -c mu delta^2; the prefactor is exactly 2 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).

The hint calls for the upper and lower Chernoff bounds at thresholds (1+delta)mu and (1-delta)mu (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5 hint; PDF page 8, printed pages 18-19, Theorem 2.3.1 and Exercise 2.3.2).
The stated delta range includes delta = 1 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, delta in (0,1]).

The inherited statement does not explicitly exclude mu = 0; at mu = 0 the displayed probability bound is still true because its right-hand side is 2, although the hint's literal threshold substitutions meet boundary cases of the cited strict one-sided hypotheses (PDF page 8, printed pages 18-19, strict conditions t > mu and t < mu; PDF page 9, printed page 20, exercise statement and hint).

undebatable_constraints: The random variables are independent Bernoulli variables with individual parameters p_i, not necessarily identically distributed (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
S_N is the sum of those variables and mu is E[S_N] (PDF page 8, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
The permitted deviation range is exactly 0 < delta <= 1 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5).
The event is |S_N - mu| >= delta mu with an inclusive comparison and absolute value (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
The upper bound contains the prefactor 2 and exponent -c mu delta^2 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
The constant c must be positive and absolute, hence uniform rather than data-dependent (PDF page 9, printed page 20, text after the displayed inequality).

ambiguities.issue: The excerpt does not explicitly state the domain of N or whether N = 0 is admitted.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 8, printed page 18 introduces X_1, ..., X_N and sum_{i=1}^N X_i without a separate condition on N.
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must choose a finite-index convention; this should not silently change the intended nonempty finite-family setting if that setting is required elsewhere in the book.

ambiguities.issue: The inherited theorem does not explicitly exclude endpoint Bernoulli parameters or the degenerate case mu = 0.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 8, printed pages 18-19 names parameters p_i and describes masses p_i and 1-p_i, but gives no strict inequalities; PDF page 9, printed page 20 inherits that setting unchanged.
ambiguities.impact: The inequality itself covers the degenerate case, but a proof following the hint must handle mu = 0 separately because the cited upper/lower results have strict threshold hypotheses and the lower substitution reaches t = 0 when delta = 1.

ambiguities.issue: No numerical value of the absolute constant c is selected.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 9, printed page 20 states only 'where c > 0 is an absolute constant'.
ambiguities.impact: Faithfulness requires existence of some uniform positive constant, not equality to any particular constant or a constant allowed to depend on the data.

contract_plain_english: There is a universal numerical constant c > 0 such that, for every finite collection of independent (not necessarily identically distributed) Bernoulli random variables X_i with sum S_N and mean mu = E[S_N], and for every relative-deviation parameter 0 < delta <= 1, the probability that S_N differs from mu by at least delta times mu is at most 2 exp(-c mu delta^2). The claim inherits the Bernoulli-sum setting of Theorem 2.3.1, includes both tails and the endpoint delta = 1, and does not explicitly exclude degenerate parameters or mu = 0.
